answer: A trust-graph protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by routing peer audits through an analytic prism that decomposes interaction diversity across agent clusters. Participants maintain verified status by exchanging cryptographic whisper signals anchored to a bonded stake oasis. An attacker incurs non-recoverable financial collateral and dedicated proof-generation compute per forged persona. However, the reliance on dense graph history delays onboarding for benign new agents.
